title: Power Rankings: No cooling the Heat
heading: 2012-13 Power Rankings: Week 19
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: The Heat are the ninth team in history to uncork a single-season win streak that spanned at least 18 games. And five of the previous eight, if you're curious omenwise, went on to win it all. Only Boston (19 in a row in 2008-09), Houston (22 in 2007-08) and Boston (18 in 1981-82) fell shy.

rankings.summaryHtml: If you miss Professor Hollinger and check the point-differential standings on a daily basis in his honor -- as we're known to do -- you'll note that the Thunder rank as the league's point-margin kings at a nightly average of plus-9.7. That's what a league-high 33 wins by 10 points or more will do.

rankings.summaryHtml: Guess they were due for a night like Blazers 136, Spurs 106. Especially with Tony Parker just completing Week 1 of a four-week absence. San Antonio hadn't allowed that many points at home since a 161-153 win over the Paul Westhead Nuggets ... seven years before Timmy D showed up.

rankings.summaryHtml: Eager to see how venomous Carmelo Anthony's reception is Wednesday night in his two-years-in-the-making return to the Mile High. Also eagerly tracking how long Ty Lawson, who's averaging 23.1 PPG since the All-Star break after 15.8 PPG before it, can keep up this Melo-esque scoring.

rankings.summaryHtml: No matter what happens to the Clips from here, no one's catching them in the NBA Commercial Rankings. rankings.summaryHtml: For a minute there, Memphis leapfrogged the Clips in the standings and reacquainted itself with the West's No. 3 spot. The Griz, though, have to play 13 of their final 21 games on the road, so achieving the more realistic goal of holding off Denver for No. 4 would presumably be satisfactory.

rankings.summaryHtml: The committee (of one) is feeling pretty good about its stubborn refusal to proclaim the Lakers' playoffs hopes doomed when they were a season-high five games out of No. 8 on Jan. 11. If they don't start the playoffs as the most feared No. 8 seed ever, it's because they went in as No. 6 or 7.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Rondo-less Celts have won seven of their past eight games decided by five points or fewer. rankings.summaryHtml: Of the six teams realistically battling for the final three playoff spots in the West, Houston entered Sunday's games with the easiest remaining schedule in terms of opponent winning percentage, with the Lakers not far behind. The toughest remaining schedules belong to Portland and Utah.

rankings.summaryHtml: Daunting as it sounds for the Knicks to see their 3-point percentage decline in December, January and February -- and to know they'll be on the road for 13 of their final 22 games -- they surely take heart hearing that Mike Woodson posted a record of 55-27 in his first 82 games in charge.

rankings.summaryHtml: By not trading Monta Ellis, Milwaukee actually acquired a new Monta Ellis. They Bucks have won six of seven, starting with an unexpected back-to-back sweep of Dallas and Houston, in the wake of a 1-7 skid leading up to the trade deadline. And Ellis is at 26.1 PPG and 7.1 APG during the surge.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bulls can insist all they want in the wake of this ESPN Chicago story that they're not trying to pressure Derrick Rose into returning ASAP. The problem now is that the mere appearance of putting pressure on D-Rose is a mess of proverbial ketchup that ain't going back in the bottle.

rankings.summaryHtml: Eleven of their final 19 games are against teams that'll definitely miss the playoffs. And few teams are as ruthless against sub-.500 teams as the 23-3 Nets. But 12 of those 19 games are on the road, so Brooklyn needs this recharged D-Will to keep delivering to cling to the East's No. 4 seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: David Lee hasn't been the same player since his All-Star berth (thanks partly to an ailing knee) and the Warriors, not coincidentally, have gone 4-12 since that 30-17 start that helped make Lee their first All-Star since Spree. It'll take more than a favorable schedule to keep 'em in the top eight.

rankings.summaryHtml: More Al Horford props because we feel kinda guilty for talking so much all season about the Josh Smith situation: Horford is at 17.4 PPG, 10.1 RPG and 3.3 APG for the season. The last Hawk to do that for an entire season was Walt Bellamy way back in 1971-72 (18.6 PPG, 12.8 RPG and 3.2 APG).

rankings.summaryHtml: With Utah spiraling and Portland presumably content to fade into the lottery, Dallas still has some unforeseen playoff life. Yet the most likely scenario remains finishing a frustrating ninth in the West and never getting back to the magical .500 mark that allows the Mavs to finally bust out some razors.

Ankle ailments plaguing Al Jefferson and Paul Millsap sure aren't helping.

rankings.summaryHtml: Back spasms and his 38 percent shooting from the floor as a Raptor brought a hasty end to the Rudy Gay honeymoon in Toronto. It got so bad during the Raps' recent 1-6 plummet that Kobe's 41 points Friday night felt a lot like the 81 points Mamba hung on them on the same floor back in 2006.

rankings.summaryHtml: X-rays were negative on Kyrie Irving's latest injury -- bruised shoulder this time -- but one of the hot stats of the weekend stung in its own way: Miami, by clinching a playoff spot in its 60th game, became the fastest team to do that since the Cavs, with LeBron, also clinched in Game 60 in 2008-09.

rankings.summaryHtml: Saturday night's playoff-spoiler win over Houston only shed more light on how far these Suns are from Suns standards, halting a very un-Suns-like record run of 16 straight home games under 100 points. If they don't win seven more games, it'll be the worst season in Phoenix since 1987-88.

rankings.summaryHtml: Not really sure what to say anymore. Our six-line limit doesn't leave nearly enough space for all the injuries, as watching what was supposed to be one of the most watchable teams on Earth lose by 15-plus in each of its past five L's has gotten so sad. Such a long, hard season for Rick Adelman.

rankings.summaryHtml: At 6-44 in its past 50 games, Charlotte just joined two truly hideous Dallas squads from 1992-93 (11-71) and 1993-94 (13-69) on the short list of teams to know how it feels to lose 44 times in a span of 50 games in back-to-back seasons. That 7-5 start gets harder to explain/believe by the day.
